body:
A line declaring a public Gleam function with a return type (`pub fn name(arg: T) -> R {`) is mistaken for a case arm when Solace finds what Gleam code refers to. `language::gleam.is_arm` only excludes lines starting with `fn`, not `pub fn`.

Confirmed by reading the code, not by running it. Likely effects:
- the function's own name counts as a local name inside its body, so a recursive call to itself isn't seen as a use of the function;
- parameter names (`arg:`) are recorded as field reads.

Fix: such lines are no longer treated as case arms. A test shows a recursive public function with a return type is found as a use of itself, and its parameters aren't recorded as field reads.
title: gleam refs: public functions aren't case arms
